## 🔴 High Relevance (Score 7–10)

**[The COX2-PGE2-PKA axis suppresses antiviral immunity by inhibiting mtDNA-dependent STING activation.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118154)** *(from Virology / lipid mediator biology (eicosanoid signaling) and mitochondrial quality control)*  
*V. Pham; Julien Cicero; Zi-Chen Wang; Hiroyuki Hakozaki; Thomas S. Hoang* — Cell reports 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, ISG15-mitophagy, treatment-target, other`  
> The paper shows that PGE2-EP4-PKA signaling drives PINK1-mediated mitophagy (via STOML2 Ser29 phosphorylation) to clear damaged mitochondria and reduce cytosolic mtDNA-driven STING and IFN-I activation. This maps directly onto the BLUE stream (mtDNA to cGAS-STING to IFN-I) and the RED stream (ISG15/ISGylation-mediated PINK1/Parkin mitophagy block) in SAMHD1 A565T haploinsufficiency. It offers a new mitophagy-enhancing, COX2/PGE2-based treatment angle, but it is HSV-1 infection-based, contains no SAMHD1 data, and its effect (suppressing antiviral STING) is the opposite of what would be wanted in an interferonopathy. The PGE2-PKA pathway might still be exploited to dampen chronic STING activation, and COX2 inhibition would carry risks.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118154

**[STING engages PKR to drive lysosomal cell death in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42874584/)** *(from Pulmonology / critical care and transplant medicine (lung ischemia-reperfusion injury))*  
*Gao Peigen; Wang Tao; Liu Yingjian; Zhuang Fenghui; Li Chongwu* — Molecular cell 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NF-kB-IKK, mTOR-lysosomal, treatment-target, other`  
> Shows that mtDNA release activates cGAS-STING, which engages PKR (Ser33 autophosphorylation) to drive IKK-NF-κB signaling independent of TBK1/IRF3, then LAMP3-mediated lysosomal membrane permeabilization and cell death. This is a novel STING-to-NF-κB route that could amplify the Loop A/NF-κB axis and link to lysosomal failure in the SAMHD1 haploinsufficiency model, though there is no SAMHD1, NLRP3 or dNTP data and the context is lung ischemia-reperfusion injury.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.molcel.2026.09.024
